body:
## Summary

Replaces the mint-and-store-JWT pattern with cookie-only delegation. auth.romaine.life owns the session via a \`.romaine.life\`-scoped cookie that the browser auto-attaches on every request to workout.romaine.life. The backend forwards the cookie to auth.romaine.life's \`/api/auth/get-session\` on each request (cached 60s) and gates on the returned role claim.

## Why now

Tank-operator's mint-local-JWT pattern was justified for tank-operator (it bundles per-user profile data into the token, making reads self-contained). For kill-me there's nothing equivalent to bundle — the JWT just re-signed the same \`{sub, email, name, role}\` auth.romaine.life already issues. The per-app KV secret + role assignments + localStorage token were all dead weight.

Per [tank-operator/docs/quality-timeframes.md](https://github.com/nelsong6/tank-operator/blob/main/docs/quality-timeframes.md): *"the durable data model or state ownership is explicit"* and *"local UI state that can contradict durable state"* — auth.romaine.life is the durable owner; the localStorage JWT was shadow state with TTL drift.

**Also fixes the prod-503 state**: pod no longer reads \`kill-me-jwt-signing-secret\`, so the workload-identity-scope-on-renamed-secret problem (which was blocked by the kill-me tfstate lock from a prior failed apply) is moot.

## Pattern

- **Backend** ([backend/auth.js](backend/auth.js)): \`createRequireAuth()\` returns middleware that:
  1. Reads \`req.headers.cookie\`
  2. Looks up the cookie in a 60s in-process cache; on miss, calls \`auth.romaine.life/api/auth/get-session\` with the cookie forwarded as the \`Cookie\` header
  3. Caches the result (positive or negative) for 60s
  4. Gates on \`role ∈ {admin, user}\` — \`pending\` returns 403
  5. Attaches \`req.user = { sub, email, name, role }\`
- **Frontend** ([frontend/src/auth/index.js](frontend/src/auth/index.js)): exposes \`bootstrapAuth()\` (calls \`/api/auth/me\` which is the unauthenticated probe), \`startLogin()\` (redirect), \`logout()\`. No token storage, no Authorization header.
- **API calls**: \`apiFetch\` sets \`credentials: 'include'\` so the cookie attaches; no Bearer header.

## End-to-end deletions

| Deleted | Why |
|---|---|
| \`backend/auth-routes.js\` | No \`/api/auth/exchange\`, no logout endpoint (handled directly via auth.romaine.life) |
| \`backend/auth.js\` HS256 + jose verifier | Backend no longer verifies tokens; just forwards cookie |
| \`backend/config.js\` KV read | No signing secret needed |
| \`jose\` + \`jsonwebtoken\` deps | Not used |
| \`frontend/src/auth/index.js\` token dance | localStorage tokens / fetchUpstreamJWT / exchange — all gone |
| \`frontend/src/api/client.js\` Authorization header | Cookie-attached automatically |
| \`tofu/keyvault.tf\` | No per-app signing secret to provision |
| \`tofu/identity.tf\` KV role assignment | Pod doesn't read KV anymore |

## Guard

[scripts/check-removed-msal.mjs](scripts/check-removed-msal.mjs) extended to block reintroduction of: \`jsonwebtoken\`, \`jose\`, \`jwt.sign\`/\`jwt.verify\`, \`createRemoteJWKSet\`, \`/api/auth/exchange\`, \`localStorage.{get,set,remove}Item('token')\`, \`kill-me-jwt-signing-secret\`.

## Sequencing

1. Merge → backend image rebuilds + ArgoCD rolls → pod boots without trying to read the missing-permission KV secret → \`workout.romaine.life\` health 200
2. Tofu apply on merge destroys the now-unused \`kill-me-jwt-signing-secret\` KV secret + the related role assignment. (If the prior tfstate lock from \`runner@runnervmrw5os 2026-05-16 05:31:06\` hasn't expired, may need one force-unlock before this apply succeeds.)

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` (frontend) clean
- [x] \`node scripts/check-removed-msal.mjs\` clean
- [ ] After image rolls: \`curl https://workout.romaine.life/health\` returns 200
- [ ] Sign in via auth.romaine.life → \`/api/auth/me\` returns user object → SPA renders signed-in
- [ ] Admin writes (log workout, edit cycle day) go through with valid cookie
- [ ] Sign out → cookie cleared on auth.romaine.life → next \`/api/auth/me\` returns null
